analyst_view.overall: FC Porto have won all ten league games (30 points, five clear of Benfica) and beat Napoli 4-1 in the Champions League this week. Francesco Farioli gets winger Oskar Pietuszewski back from a thigh injury, while William Gomes is doubtful and Smalling and Vasco Sousa are still out. Vitória are 13th with 9 points, just two clear of the relegation zone.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Porto are in irresistible form and Pietuszewski's return adds a threat out wide, but Vitória have been tight at the back recently (only five conceded in their last six by the site's count) and Guimarães is a tough away ground. These point in opposite directions, so we stay close to the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, split almost evenly. A Porto side this dominant, with Pietuszewski back to take on full-backs, should pin a struggling Vitória back for long spells, which tends to bring Porto corners. We lean slightly above the site's total.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards. Vitória against Porto is usually a heated fixture, and a home side near the bottom will need to stop Porto's wingers. Referee David Silva has been named, but we found nothing about his style this season, so we stay with the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots. Porto should take more shots than the near-even split the site suggests, but Vitória are likely to sit deeper and shoot less. The total probably ends up close to the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target. Porto's attack is sharp after the 4-1 against Napoli, but Vitória's recent defensive record argues against a big number. We have no strong reason to move from the site.
